add.issue.name: CLI and shell assume the repo lives at ~/Aphotic-Hypr

edit.description.md:
A checkout cloned under any other name or letter case (for example `~/aphotic-hypr`) breaks two things:

- `aphotic sync` fails because the CLI looks for `~/Aphotic-Hypr`.
- Settings > About shows `…` instead of the version, because the pane reads `~/Aphotic-Hypr/VERSION`.

Fix: the CLI resolves the repo from its own location and keeps `~/.local/share/aphotic/dots` pointed at it. The shell reads the repo through that link via `InstallProfile.dotsDir`, falling back to `~/Aphotic-Hypr` for installs without the link. `APHOTIC_DOTS_DIR` still overrides both.

Existing installs at a different path need one manual `git pull` and an `aphotic` run, since the old `aphotic update` cannot find the checkout.

Related: MQ38RZ6 (rename the install path).

add.issue.name: ComfyUI engine plugin: Flow, the AI tab and live generation progress in the AI notch tile

edit.description.md:
ComfyUI runs image and video generation on the GPU, and it can claim most of the card. Today the shell doesn't know it exists. Its VRAM shows up as unattributed, and nothing reports a generation's progress.

Plan:
- Ship ComfyUI as an engine plugin in the plugins repo. Core never names it. It uses the `[engine]` descriptor capability from A9Q1R0G.
- Core registers its VRAM as a GPU claim, the same way loaded llama-swap models are claimed. Flow draws it, and the resource engine and inference mode count it. A ComfyUI started by hand is attributed by its process.
- On a llama-swap host, ComfyUI runs as a llama-swap entry, so it shares the GPU with language models under one arbiter. A swap to ComfyUI shows it as the active engine.
- The AI tab lists it with its controls.
- The AI notch tile shows the running job: step N of M, steps per second, the current node, the queue length, and done, error or interrupted. The data comes from ComfyUI's websocket. One connection is open while the engine runs, and nothing polls at idle.

Depends on A9Q1R0G (engine descriptors). The design adds an engine-agnostic job-progress capability, so other generators can feed the same tile.

add.issue.name: GPU claims stack instead of handing off, and contention warnings repeat

edit.description.md:
Flow reported 37000 MB of VRAM claimed while the GPU held one process using about 500 MB. Claims from llama-swap and llama.cpp aren't released when a model swaps or a process exits, so they pile up. Every new contention episode sends another "over budget" notification, and users have seen five or more in a row.

Plan:
- Find each claim that outlives its process or model, release it at the source, and cover it with a test.
- One notification per resource per episode, with a short settle window, so a swap doesn't re-fire it.
- Add a "Don't warn about this again" action on the notification, chosen by the user and undone in Settings. Flow still shows the contention. Nothing is muted automatically.

Contention episodes key on resource plus holders and stay open for 15 s after clearing, so a swap doesn't notify twice. #351 adds a read-only capture script, which showed inference mode stuck on with no model. edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Opening the Agent Memory workspace draws a black plane. `MemoryWorkspace.qml` uses `Colours` without `import qs.services`, so every colour binding throws a ReferenceError and falls back to opaque black. **Plan.**
- Add the missing import and bind the tab bar's index back to the plane.
- Add an offscreen probe that instantiates the real workspace against a folded fixture and fails on ReferenceError/TypeError or an unlit palette.
- Add `tools/check_qml_imports.py`: it finds every core singleton by `pragma Singleton` and fails any plugin file that uses one without importing its module. It runs across all plugins.

add.issue.name: Agent Memory learns from repeated failures and feeds lessons back to every harness

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The hooks record that a tool failed but not why, so every failing shell command folds into one signature and the memory cannot tell a missing `jq` from a rejected push. The digest only reaches one harness's instruction file, and nothing turns a repeated failure into a rule an agent reads.

**Plan.**
- Hooks: on a tool failure, record a short local `error` object: the command's first word, the exit code, and the first error line (max 160 chars) with tokens, keys, emails and the home prefix scrubbed. Nothing leaves the machine.
- Fold: signatures come from tool + command + normalized error line. Store v2 with a migration.
- Lessons: an issue seen 3+ times across 2+ sessions becomes a candidate. The user promotes it with one line of rule text. The plugin never writes a rule on its own. Lessons can also be imported read-only from sources declared in a drop-in file (agent memory folders, markdown files with `**Rule:**` lines). A later failure that matches a lesson counts a hit, which shows a rule that is not reaching agents.
- Feedback: a harness descriptor declares its instruction file. The digest (lessons by hits, then top unexplained failures, about 30 lines) is injected per harness, only where the user turns it on, between markers.
- Workspace: Issues, Lessons, Notes, Tools and Sources tabs, a Promote action, and per-harness injection toggles.

**Done when** two different shell failures fold into two issues with their messages, a promoted lesson appears in each opted-in harness file, and turning it off removes only the marked block.

add.issue.name: Skills: Adopt imports every agent's skills into one library, with sets you switch per session

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Adopt runs the skills CLI with no paths, and the CLI refuses ("provide at least one path to scan"), so the library stays empty. The CLI already supports a central library, linked deploys and additive presets, but the plugin exposes none of it. Users who install many skills cannot keep them off until a session needs them.

**Plan.**
- Find every skill folder: a shipped list of known global locations (`~/.agents`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.omp`, `~/.pi` and others), every installed agent's folder as the CLI reports it, and a user drop-in list. Only existing folders count.
- Adopt runs as preview, then confirm, then import. Before anything moves, the source folders are backed up. Originals are replaced by the library's managed links, so turning a skill off really removes it from that agent. Links into git checkouts are left alone and listed. Broken links are reported.
- Sets: the CLI's presets shown as Sets (UI, Code, Review, ...) with a live on/off toggle, plus `aphotic skills set on|off <name>` for starting a session.

**Done when** a sandbox test proves backup, import and set toggling on a throwaway home, and the plane shows a preview and waits for a yes before touching real folders.

Spine becomes the default and takes the details only Performance had (temps, storage, battery, upload, GPU switch). Performance hides while Spine is active and stays for Classic. Flow keeps only VRAM claims. Every tab moves onto shared card, label and readout parts and one fixed stage size.

add.issue.name: Agents tile: steady with several live harnesses, a session switcher, stats for every harness

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** With several harnesses running at once (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, pi, omp), the Agents notch tile flips its headline between them about once a second. Only Claude gets rich stats. There is no way to jump from the tile to a running session.

**Plan.** Pick the headline harness with a stable rule (waiting-for-input first, then the most recent real phase change, held for a minimum dwell) instead of whichever event arrived last. Add a switcher: one clickable chip per live harness session, idle or busy, that focuses that session's window. Show the same stat set for every harness that reports it (phase, model, tokens, subagents, cost or quota where the harness exposes it), and say plainly when a harness reports less.

**Done when.** Four harnesses running at once give a headline that changes only on a real state change, every live session has a chip that focuses its window, and each harness shows every stat its events carry.

add.issue.name: Docker notch tile: containers, compose projects and the daemon at a glance

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The Dev layer has no view of Docker. Checking whether a container is up, restarting one or tailing its logs means a terminal.

**Plan.** A new `docker` plugin with a notch tile under the `dev` layer. It shows daemon state, containers grouped by compose project with state, uptime, ports and CPU/memory, and offers start, stop, restart, open logs in a terminal and open a shell. Disk use comes from `docker system df`. Prune asks first. The tile polls only while it is on screen.

**Done when.** With the daemon running, every container appears with its state, start/stop/restart work and settle in the tile, and a closed notch runs no docker command.

add.issue.name: Games notch tile: now playing, recent games and one-click launch

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The Games tile is a row of store-client buttons. It does not show what is running, cannot launch a game directly, and says nothing about what the Gaming profile is doing for the session.

**Plan.** Extend the game-launcher tile. While a game runs: its name, time played, and chips for gamemode, do-not-disturb and the VRAM a local model gave up. Otherwise: the most recently played games and pinned favourites as one-click launch tiles, then the client row and a button that opens the library plane. Everything reads the service's last scan; opening the notch starts no scan.

**Done when.** A running game shows in the tile with its elapsed time, a recent game launches from the tile, and the tile reads nothing new from disk when opened.

add.issue.name: Security notch tile: exposure, VPN and the engagement in progress

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The Security layer has a profile but no surface in the notch, so its state is invisible until something goes wrong.

**Plan.** A `security-notch-tile` plugin under the `security` layer that answers "how exposed is this machine right now": VPN state with a connect/disconnect toggle, services listening on a non-loopback address, firewall state, active inbound SSH sessions, and the count of packages with known vulnerabilities from the last audit. It shows an engagement in progress with its elapsed time and start/end buttons wired to the Security profile. The tile polls only while it is on screen and never acts without a click.

**Done when.** The tile lists every non-loopback listener, toggles the VPN, and starts and ends an engagement through the profile.

add.issue.name: Widgets plugin: resizable Signal desktop widgets

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The desktop has no widgets. Clocks, calendars, media, system meters and timers live only inside shell surfaces.

**Plan.** A `widgets` plugin that draws transparent, Signal-styled widgets on the desktop layer. Each widget can be placed, resized and configured, and the plugin ships a large catalog in its first release: clocks, date and calendar, media, system meters, weather, productivity timers and notes. Core gains one small seam: an overlay may hand the shell a mask made of several regions, so the desktop between widgets keeps taking clicks.

**Done when.** Widgets can be added from a catalog, dragged, resized, configured and removed, layout survives a restart, and the empty desktop between them still takes clicks.

add.issue.name: aphotic sync deploys the newest release tag on an edge install

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `aphotic sync` runs `install.sh --config-only` without a channel. install.sh defaults to `stable` and does not read the channel saved in `~/.local/state/aphotic/channel`, so it checks out the newest `vX.Y.Z` tag before deploying. On a machine following `dev` (edge), Settings → About's update button and `aphotic sync --no-pull` both quietly move the checkout back to the last release and deploy that. Nothing says so, and a diff of the live config against the checkout afterwards passes because both are the tag.

**Plan.** install.sh reads the saved channel when `--channel` is not given, and `aphotic sync` passes the saved channel through explicitly. The sync log names the channel and the ref it deployed.

**Done when.** On an edge install, `aphotic sync --no-pull` leaves the checkout on the commit it started on and deploys it; on a stable install it still deploys the newest tag.

add.issue.name: Dashboard: live tiles that fill the stage

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Dashboard tabs sat at their own small size in the middle of a large frame (Workspaces read as one small tile in a big window), the CPU ridge was a jagged canvas line with no rounded edges, and the clock opened with a fuzzy, noisy outline.

**Plan.** Every tab fills the stage. The Dashboard tab becomes a grid of live Signal tiles sized in cells, each with one moving part that moves only when its value does. Workspaces becomes a live map of each workspace's windows. Curves become smooth antialiased paths in rounded, outlined wells, and the clock is plain crisp text.

**Done when.** Every tab reaches the frame's edges, the Dashboard tab is the tile grid, and the remaining tabs (Flow, Wallpapers, AI Chat) are rebuilt on the same tile.

add.issue.name: Canary: a comment mentioning install_software is read as a package named "runs"

edit.description.md:
The nightly install canary has failed every day since 2026-10-19 (issue #373) with "No AUR package found for runs". No package called `runs` exists in the installer. The canary collects installer packages by grepping for `install_software <word>`, and a comment in the fonts installer reads "install_software runs one pacman transaction per package", so the word `runs` lands in the package list.

Fix: skip lines where `install_software` follows a `#`, and add a `--list` mode to the canary script so a test can check the resolved package list without touching pacman.

add.issue.name: Bar: every style renders fully when docked left or right

edit.description.md:
Switching the bar between top, bottom, left and right works, but several styles clip, squeeze or warp their entries on a side dock. The taskbar and minimal styles always lay out one row, so docked to a side the row overflows the strip and the wrapper clips it. Their popout hit-testing reads only the x axis, too.

Outcome: all five styles render every entry at all four orientations, with a geometry test that builds each style at its real strip size and fails on any clipped or squeezed child. Follow-ups: reproduce the capsule Bluetooth clip with live device state, and a motion pass on the orientation switch.

add.issue.name: Headless inference mode: no shell or compositor while logged out

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** A machine running Aphotic keeps a greeter, compositor and shell resident even when nobody is logged in. Someone who also uses the box as an inference server loses RAM, VRAM and CPU to a desktop nobody is looking at.

**Plan.**
- A systemd target for headless inference. It conflicts with the display manager, starts the engine named by an engine descriptor (no engine named in core), and keeps sshd and tailscaled running.
- `aphotic inference up` enters it from the greeter, a TTY or SSH. It refuses while a graphical session is open, so it never closes anyone's apps.
- `aphotic inference down` returns to graphical.target and the login screen.
- `aphotic inference status` reports the mode, the engine, and its RAM and VRAM use.
- Install profiles ship the unit files. Nothing switches modes on its own.

**Done when.** On the dev VM and on a real GPU host: `up` from a TTY leaves no compositor, greeter or shell process and serves requests from the configured engine. `down` brings the greeter back. `up` from inside a desktop session refuses with a clear message. Before/after RAM and VRAM are measured and recorded.

add.issue.name: Wallpapers: theme-matched packs fetched on request, ultrawide images on 21:9 screens

edit.description.md:
Each theme shipped around a dozen wallpapers inside the repo, 107 MB in all, with no way to add a curated set without growing the repo again.

Plan:
- A `wallpaper-pack` plugin capability and user drop-ins under `~/.config/aphotic/wallpapers/`. A pack is a TOML file with a pinned `base_url` and rows of theme, path, sha256, width and height.
- `aphotic wallpaper fetch | packs | index`. Fetch writes into the theme's own folder, keeps a file only after its hash matches, and skips files already present.
- Core keeps one default wallpaper per theme. The rest move to a pack served from the repo at a pinned commit.
- `.wallpapers.json` in each theme folder records image sizes. On a 21:9 screen, theme pick, cycle and random prefer ultrawide images.
- The plugins repo ships a `wallpaper-packs` plugin with the classic pack and a curated community pack.

add.issue.name: Desktop widgets: blurred glass, real empty states, and a finish pass on every widget

edit.description.md:
Rendered offscreen, the 44 desktop widgets show three problems across the set:
- The glass never blurs. The compositor's panel blur rule does not match plugin overlays, so busy wallpapers bleed through and text loses contrast.
- Every card has an accent-colored hairline, which competes with the content.
- Empty states are a line of text in a corner: Quick Launch ships with no apps, and Bluetooth, Photo, the media widgets and Todo leave large blank cards.

Specific defects: the binary clock's dots leave their column grid and its unlit dots are invisible, Progress of the Day sets its labels around 9 px, the stopwatch sits in the top corner of its card, and a stored layout without `data` throws in five stateful widgets.

Plan: core gains an opt-in `glass = true` key on `[ui.overlay]` that puts the overlay under the compositor's blur rule. The widgets plugin turns it on, moves to a neutral hairline, adds one shared empty-state part, and fixes each defect above.

add.issue.name: Workspace panes: Agent Memory and Skills layout fixes

edit.description.md:
Rendered at 1600x900 with real data, the Agent Memory and Skills workspace panes have layout defects.

Agent Memory: the READY badge and every action button have no width, so their text overlaps neighbours and the Add note button runs off the edge. The Issues/Lessons/Notes/Tools tabs draw as unstyled default controls. The context digest never wraps. The project line prints raw `sessions=7 turns=49`. Issue cards are a fixed height and clip their buttons.

Skills: with the CLI missing, the pane dumps the CLI's raw output, machine paths included, and repeats the message in the middle. The search placeholder is dark on dark.

Fix each in place and keep both plugins' probes passing.

add.issue.name: Appearance: window opacity slider, applied live

edit.description.md:
A user asked how to change window transparency. Today it means editing Hyprland's config by hand.

Add one slider to Settings > Appearance that sets how see-through windows are. It changes Hyprland's active and inactive opacity on the running session as you drag, and saves to a small generated file Hyprland loads at start, so the choice survives a reload or reboot.

Per-app rules multiply with this value, so apps that are already more transparent stay that way relative to the rest. A hand-written value in custom.lua still wins on the next reload.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: PR #381. Settings > Appearance > Windows has a Window opacity slider from 30% to 100%. It applies to the running session through `hyprctl eval` and saves to `~/.config/hypr/appearance.lua`, which hyprland.lua loads before custom.lua. Per-app rules still multiply with it. Not tried on a live Hyprland yet.
